Mrs. Mary A. 1ferry may b)e reinstated as a printer's assistant in the
Bureau of En graving and Pri nting without regard to the length of her
separation from the service.
Mrs. Perry, after most satisfactory service, resigned from the Bureau
of Engravingw and Printing on X itgust 2J, iqio, to marry. John -l. ferry,
her husband, a plate printer emldoyed in the Bureau, died on Septembher
27, 1 915, leaving her with two small children to support. It is also neces-
sarv for her to) coiitribute ito the support of a wid1owed mother anid two
minor sisters. I t is stately that she is twenty-six years of age, highly skilled
in the work of many divisions of the Bureau, and of a type especially
desirable where the work is of an exacting mental and physical nature.
The Civil Service Commission concurs with the Actin,~ Secretary of
